subject: Automotive & EVs
title: China's EV Dominance
description: A quick win: understand China's EV Dominance.

hook.text: China sells more electric cars than the rest of the world combined. And it happened fast.

buildup.text: The government offered massive subsidies, free license plates, and built charging networks aggressively.

discovery.text: BYD, once a battery company, became the world's largest EV maker by volume in 2023.

twist.text: Chinese EVs now cost as little as $10,000—far cheaper than anything Western makers can match.

climax.text: Europe and the US are imposing tariffs, fearing Chinese EVs will dominate their markets too.

punchline.text: China didn't just join the EV race—it's leading it.

quiz.question: Which company became the world's largest EV maker by volume?

details.summary: China sells more electric vehicles than the rest of the world combined, led by BYD and supported by massive government subsidies, a dominant battery supply chain, and a competitive domestic market.
details.whyItMatters: China's dominance in EVs threatens to reshape the global auto industry. Its cost advantage in batteries and manufacturing could make Chinese EVs unbeatable on price in most world markets.
takeaways: China accounts for over 60 percent of global EV sales
BYD surpassed Tesla as the world's top EV seller in late 2023
Chinese companies control most of the global battery supply chain

faq.question: How did China become the dominant EV market?
faq.answer: Decades of government subsidies, mandated EV production quotas, investment in charging infrastructure, and domestic battery manufacturing created an ecosystem that Chinese automakers exploited with affordable, competitive products.

faq.question: Can Western automakers compete with Chinese EV prices?
faq.answer: It is extremely difficult. Chinese manufacturers have 20 to 30 percent cost advantages from cheaper labor, vertically integrated battery supply chains, and government support. Tariffs are one of the few tools Western governments can use.
